beats.vo: In this week's recap, we start with a mystery.
Two Italian engineers are dead in Kuwait, killed by a drone. Italy blames Iran. Tehran says it was a false flag.

ov.text: Two Italians killed in Kuwait drone strike

beats.vo: We'll lay out what we know, and at the end, the question no one can answer yet.
Plus, a strike claim that moved oil prices, another night of missiles over Ukraine, an ISIS attack in Syria, deadly strikes in Gaza, and a record Ebola outbreak in Congo.

segments.chapter: Drone strike in Kuwait kills two Italians
segments.src: CNN, Canberra Times, TRT World, Il Sole 24 Ore

beats.vo: Let's start in Kuwait. A drone struck an air defence detection station, where two Italian technicians working for the defence company Rheinmetall were killed.

ov.text: Two Rheinmetall Italia technicians killed

beats.vo: Kuwait's defence ministry says two other people, a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national, were injured.

Italy's foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, says the drones were Iranian, and that the drone used in the attack was made in Iran. Kuwait says the attack violated a UN Security Council resolution, and has invoked its right to self-defence.

ov.text: Italy blames Iran; Kuwait invokes right to self-defence

beats.vo: Iran denies any role. A military spokesman said its armed forces had carried out no operations in the region, and suggested the attack was a false flag, meant to escalate tensions. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told his Italian counterpart that Iran was not involved, and offered a joint investigation with Kuwait.

ov.text: Iran denies involvement, suggests a 'false flag'

beats.vo: Who launched the drones has not been independently verified.

ov.text: Responsibility not independently verified

segments.chapter: Houthis claim strike on Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery

beats.vo: Next, to Saudi Arabia, where Yemen's Houthi movement says it has struck Ras Tanura, the country's largest oil refinery.

ov.text: Houthis claim strike on Ras Tanura refinery

beats.vo: The group says the attack started fires, and satellite images showed thick black smoke rising over the site.

ov.text: Fires and smoke reported at the site

beats.vo: The Saudi-led coalition says its air defences intercepted four drones over Ras Tanura. It has not confirmed any damage to the refinery itself.
In Riyadh, a tower in the financial district was hit. Saudi civil defence says eleven people were wounded. It was the second strike on the same tower in less than a week.
Oil prices jumped after the claim. The coalition has promised a firm response, and the Houthis are threatening more attacks.

ov.text: Oil prices rise as coalition vows a firm response

beats.vo: To Ukraine, where Russia launched another large overnight barrage of ballistic missiles and drones.

ov.text: Overnight missile and drone barrage

beats.vo: Ukraine says its air defences shot down eighty-seven of them.

ov.label: missiles and drones shot down, Ukraine says

beats.vo: In Kharkiv, a drone hit a residential high-rise, killing a man and a woman. A third person was killed when another strike hit an educational building in the city.

ov.text: Kharkiv: three killed in drone and missile strikes

beats.vo: Across the country, the public broadcaster Suspilne reports at least seven people killed and fifty-eight injured.

ov.label: killed across Ukraine, at least 58 injured

beats.vo: The attack came after Vladimir Putin warned of retaliation for Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy facilities.

ov.text: Putin had vowed retaliation for strikes on Russian energy sites

segments.src: Syrian state media via The National

beats.vo: In north-east Syria, the Islamic State group attacked an internal security building in the city of Hassakeh.

ov.text: ISIS attack on security building in Hassakeh

beats.vo: Syrian state media says two members of the security forces were killed, and five were injured.
Officials say all four attackers died. Two of them were killed in clashes, and two blew themselves up.

ov.text: Four attackers dead, officials say

beats.vo: It's a reminder that ISIS cells remain active in the region, years after the group lost its territory.

ov.text: ISIS cells remain active in north-east Syria

beats.vo: In Gaza, hospital officials say Israeli strikes overnight killed eight Palestinians.
That came a day after nine people were reported killed in separate strikes.

ov.text: Nine reported killed the day before

beats.vo: A ceasefire has been in place since October 2025, but deadly strikes have repeatedly tested it. Israel has said earlier strikes were responses to militant attacks on its troops.

ov.text: Ceasefire in place since October 2025

beats.vo: And finally, to the Democratic Republic of Congo, where an Ebola outbreak has become the largest the country has ever recorded.

ov.text: Congo's largest Ebola outbreak on record

beats.vo: As of November seventeenth, Europe's disease control agency counted eleven thousand, five hundred and four confirmed cases, and five thousand, six hundred and thirty deaths.
The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, began in May. UNICEF says children make up around twenty-eight percent of confirmed cases.
Africa CDC says the outbreak is still not under control, with conflict, late detection and stretched health services slowing the response.

ov.text: Africa CDC: outbreak not under control

segments.chapter: The open question: who was behind the Kuwait strike?
segments.src: CNN, Fox News, Il Sole 24 Ore

beats.vo: That's the week. But one question still hangs over it.

ov.text: The open question

beats.vo: Italy and Kuwait say the drone that killed two Italians was Iranian. Tehran says it was a false flag.

ov.text: Italy and Kuwait blame Iran. Tehran says 'false flag'

beats.vo: Some in Iran have gone further. Mohammad Marandi, a former adviser to Iran's nuclear negotiators, claimed Ukraine could be behind it, but offered no evidence. Ukraine has sent military specialists to the Gulf to help defend against Iranian drones.

ov.text: Marandi: Ukraine could be behind it (no evidence offered)

beats.vo: Italy's foreign minister points out that many pro-Iranian militias operate in the region.

ov.text: Tajani: many pro-Iranian militias operate in the region

beats.vo: So who really launched that drone? Iran, a group it backs, or someone trying to drag Europe deeper into this conflict? Until there's an independent investigation, we may not know.

ov.text: Who was really behind the Kuwait strike?

beats.vo: Tell us what you think in the comments. And subscribe, so you don't miss next week's episode.
